title: Climate-Resilient Housing and Infrastructure in the Global South
subtitle: Modular construction, nature-based drainage, decentralized utilities, and tenure-secure adaptation across the 21st century
description: A century-scale framework (2000–2100) arguing that resilient housing and infrastructure for informal settlements rests on four pillars (envelope, hydrology, utilities and tenure), in twelve chapters from structural hardening and flood defense to slope stabilization, early warning, tenure and financing.
contribution: A twelve-chapter monograph on climate-resilient housing and infrastructure for informal settlements, built on four pillars (envelope, hydrology, utilities and tenure): hardening against wind and flood, sponge drainage, off-grid utilities, slopes, early warning, tenure governance and micro-finance, with a lexicon of its own terms.
abstract: Climate-resilient housing and infrastructure are presented as a way to decouple the survival of people in informal settlements from compounding climate disasters. The monograph argues that low-quality housing and missing drainage make routine storms recurrently destructive, and proposes four pillars (envelope, hydrology, utilities and tenure) combining hardened and vernacular construction, flood-elevated and amphibious foundations, nature-based drainage, off-grid power and water, slope bioengineering, early warning, secure tenure and micro-finance.

The monograph is organised in twelve chapters covering the macroeconomic anatomy of housing and infrastructure risk, multi-hazard structural engineering, hydrological defense, nature-based drainage, thermal envelope and vernacular materials, decentralized utilities, slope stabilization, early warning and monitoring, land tenure governance, financing and cross-regional field deployments, and closes with a century-scale synthesis across four planning periods from 2000 to 2100. It includes a lexicon of the framework’s defined terms.
coreProposition: Resilient housing and infrastructure for informal settlements, built on four pillars of envelope, hydrology, utilities and tenure, can decouple population survivability from compounding climate disasters.

keyFindings.title: A recurring disaster trap.
keyFindings.text: The monograph argues that scrap-metal roofs, weak foundations and missing drainage turn routine storms into repeated disasters that consume a large share of household income, and that a large infrastructure financing gap sustains this trap for over a billion people.

keyFindings.title: Hardening and flood defense.
keyFindings.text: It proposes continuous load paths, aerodynamic hip roofs, engineered bamboo and confined masonry against wind and earthquakes, and plinth elevation, stilts and amphibious foundations against flooding.

keyFindings.title: Sponge drainage and slopes.
keyFindings.text: It proposes vegetated bioswales, retention wetlands and mangrove buffers in place of clogged ditches, and vetiver grass and crib-walls to stabilize hillsides.

keyFindings.title: Off-grid utilities and early warning.
keyFindings.text: It proposes rooftop solar microgrids, rainwater cisterns and biodigesters for continuity of services, and low-cost sensor networks and cell-broadcast alerts for warnings.

keyFindings.title: Tenure and finance.
keyFindings.text: It argues that insecure tenure keeps households from investing in their homes, and proposes occupancy pacts and community land trusts together with revolving trusts, utility pay-as-you-save and parametric insurance for packages of roughly $100 to $500.

keyFindings.title: Field deployments and a century in four periods.
keyFindings.text: It draws on programs in Dhaka, Beira, Medellín, Nairobi and Jakarta, and sets out a strategy through the unserviced slum era (2000–2025), standardized micro-infrastructure (2025–2050), amphibious systems and microgrids (2050–2075) and universal resilience parity (2075–2100).

glossary.definition: The proactive application of economic development, technological diffusion, and institutional strengthening to reduce interconnected risks threatening human survivability.
The trap wherein chronic municipal under-investment in drainage and foundations forces slums to repeatedly spend scarce capital on disaster rebuilding rather than productive growth.
A proposed institutional elasticity metric quantifying the percentage of available adaptation capital that a household or municipality actually deploys into durable physical improvements.

A structural engineering design principle ensuring that wind uplift, seismic shear, and flood buoyancy are transferred without interruption from roof ridge to ground foundations without joint separation.
A four-slope roof configuration (pitched at 25°–35°) that deflects cyclone air currents, described as reducing net aerodynamic uplift suction forces by up to 55% compared to gable or flat roofs.
A foundation system that rests on ground plinths during dry periods but floats vertically on rising floodwaters along vertical steel guidance pylons, preventing interior inundation.

An ecological civil engineering approach using vegetated bioswales, retention wetlands, and permeable strata to absorb and slow stormwater runoff, described as reducing peak flood discharges by more than 65%.

A high-density structural masonry block manufactured by subjecting subsoil mixtures to mechanical hydraulic compression (above 10 MPa), offering high thermal mass with 85% less carbon than fired brick.
Large-diameter structural bamboo culms borate-treated against fungal rot and connected via mortar-injected node joints, described as delivering steel-grade tensile capacity at 60% lower cost.
An autonomous energy system (rooftop solar PV, LiFePO4 batteries, and DC distribution) capable of disconnecting from central grids to maintain 95% or more operational uptime during disasters.
A gravity-fed water purification column using engineered sand strata and a biological active layer (schmutzdecke), described as removing 98% of pathogens without electricity or chemical chlorine.
The ratio of available soil shear strength to shear stress along a hillside failure plane; slopes with FoS below 1.0 collapse, whereas vetiver bioengineering is said to maintain FoS above 1.5.
The application of Chrysopogon zizanioides grass whose 4.5-meter deep roots (85 MPa tensile strength) act as living soil nails, anchoring unstable hillside topsoil.
A low-power, long-range wireless radio communication protocol operating on open industrial bands, transmitting environmental sensor data across 15 km without commercial cellular grids.
A proposed municipal covenant granting informal settlement residents immunity from eviction for 5 to 10 years conditioned upon the execution of verified physical resilience upgrades.
An emergency disaster liquidity mechanism that automatically executes cash payouts to community groups within 48 hours based on independently verified satellite weather triggers.
